description:
You are a geometry professor preparing an interactive GeoGebra applet demonstrating the Simson Line theorem. Construct the following in GeoGebra:

1. Triangle vertices at specific coordinates: A = (0, 0), B = (6, 0), C = (2, 5)
2. The triangle polygon (or sides as lines)
3. The circumcircle of triangle ABC (the unique circle passing through all three vertices)
4. A moveable point P constrained to the circumcircle
5. Perpendicular projections from P onto each of the three sides (or lines containing the sides) of the triangle, producing three foot points
6. The Simson Line — a line passing through the perpendicular foot points (they are collinear because P lies on the circumcircle)
7. A text annotation mentioning 'Simson Line' or describing the collinearity property

Save the construction as 'simson_line.ggb' in ~/Documents/GeoGebra/projects/
